$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.haxe.expressions. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-PSE-USING-INSERT-SILENT
arms.note: the merged `using` insert answers `true` whether or not it was appended, so `prefer-static-extension` keeps rewrites whose declaration never landed

arms.name: M-FACTS-FIXED-CAPTURE
arms.note: no constructor capture counts as fixed, so a capture typed closed stays report-only

arms.name: M-FACTS-FIXED-LOOP
arms.note: no loop binder counts as fixed, so a binder over a call with a closed result stays report-only

arms.name: M-FACTS-FIXED-ANY-BINDER
arms.find: if (decl == null || !FactsBindings.fixedAt(oracle, file, root, decl, s.shape)) return Verdict.UnresolvedReceiver;
arms.note: every inferred binding is asked of the facts, so a receiver a later call typed is rewritten and no longer compiles

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-INFERRED
arms.note: an unannotated local, whose type the rewritten call itself may have bound, is typed by the facts

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-OFF
arms.note: a receiver only the compiler's facts type stays report-only

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-SHADOW
arms.find: for (id in chain) if (facts.type(id)?.fields.exists(f -> f.name == method) == true) return Shadowed;
arms.note: a same-name member of a supertype or an interface no longer drops the site

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-HOSTS
arms.note: a forwarding abstract counts as a member host whose own fields are its members

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-USING
arms.note: a receiver type's own @:using, which wins over the file's, is ignored

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-PARAM
arms.note: an abstract first parameter, reached through @:from, is taken as accepting the receiver

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-OVERLOAD
arms.note: an overloaded static is judged by its first signature, the only one the facts field records

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-DYNAMIC
arms.note: a Dynamic receiver is reported instead of dropped

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-NULL
arms.note: a nullable receiver is read as the Null abstract, which hosts no member

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-TEXT
arms.note: facts of the text the compile read answer for a file edited since

arms.name: M-PSE-FIRST-PARAM
arms.note: the last parameter of a facts signature is read as its first

arms.name: M-PSE-CHANNEL-ALIAS
arms.note: a module name an import alias rebinds to another type keeps the site as a candidate

arms.name: M-PSE-CHANNEL-REGION-USING
arms.replace: for (child in node.children) if (child.kind != 'Conditional') collectUsings(child, out);
arms.note: a using inside a conditional region is invisible to the conflict gate

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-USING-MODULE-WIDE
arms.note: the facts weigh only the type a using names, not the rest of its module

arms.name: M-PSE-FACTS-USING-SELF-MODULE
arms.note: the facts do not weigh the other types of the configured module

arms.name: M-SUBSTR-ANY-START
arms.note: every substr start is flagged, not only a subtraction

arms.name: M-RCMP-ANY-OPERAND-TYPE
arms.note: every operand type is accepted, so a Float chain, which answers 0 for a NaN where Reflect.compare answers a sign, is rewritten

arms.name: M-RCMP-IMPURE-OPERAND
arms.note: an operand that runs code is accepted, so a call the chain evaluates twice is evaluated once by the rewrite

arms.name: M-RCMP-ANY-TERMINAL
arms.note: any closing value is accepted, so a chain that answers something other than 0 for equal operands is rewritten

arms.name: M-RCMP-ANY-CALL
arms.note: every two-parameter function literal passed to any call is read as a comparator, whose exact -1 / 1 a caller outside a sort may read

arms.name: M-RCMP-ANY-NONNULL
arms.note: every chain is rewritten, so one that answers 0 for a null operand is rewritten into a call that answers -1

arms.name: M-RCMP-NAMED-TARGET-NULL
arms.find: noFix: called.nonNull || compare != null ? null : MAY_BE_NULL
arms.note: a chain whose target is the project's named function is reported without a fix on a null caveat that belongs to Reflect.compare

arms.name: M-RCMP-MIXED-OPERANDS
arms.note: the right operand's type is not compared, so an Int against a Float is rewritten into a call that does not compile

arms.name: M-RCMP-NONNULL-EITHER
arms.note: one proved operand is enough, so a chain whose other operand may be null is rewritten into a call that answers differently

arms.name: M-RCMP-BARE-ANY-ORDER
arms.note: any two operands count as the parameters in order, so a swapped comparison loses its lambda and the sort turns over

arms.name: M-RCMP-BARE-NOT-WHOLE
arms.note: a chain closing a longer body replaces the whole callback, so the statements before it are deleted

arms.name: M-RCMP-MOVE-IGNORED
arms.note: a Reflect.compare call in a callback is never moved to the function the project names

arms.name: M-RCMP-BARE-ANY-ELEMENT
arms.note: the element type is not read, so a bare Reflect.compare over any array moves to the Int function and does not compile

arms.name: M-RCMP-ANY-NAMED
arms.note: the chain operand type does not pick the function, so an Int chain is rewritten to the String function

arms.name: M-RCMP-MOVE-NONNULL
arms.note: a moved call is fixed without a proof of non-null, where Reflect.compare and the typed function answer differently

arms.name: M-RCMP-IMPORT-LOST
arms.note: the fix writes the short name of the function and no import of its type, so the file stops compiling

arms.name: M-RCMP-UNRESOLVED-SILENT
arms.find: problems.push('$label: the resolution index declares no "$path"');
arms.note: a name the index cannot find is dropped in silence and the rule falls back to Reflect.compare

arms.name: M-RCMP-PRIVATE-TYPE
arms.note: a private type is accepted as the home of the function, so the fix writes an import or a path that does not compile

arms.name: M-RCMP-FILE-SCOPED
arms.note: the configured path resolves to nothing, as it did whenever the scanned file held a guarded or unread import of the package

arms.name: M-RCMP-ANY-SIGNATURE
arms.note: any declaration of the name is accepted, so the fix writes a call that does not compile or does not compare

arms.name: M-RCMP-ERROR-NO-FILE
arms.note: the configuration error stands on no file, where the per-file gate reads a default-off rule as off and drops it from every normal run

arms.name: M-RCMP-ERROR-FIRST-FILE
arms.note: the error stays on the first file seen, which the gate drops when the rule is off there though it is on elsewhere

arms.name: M-RCMP-MOVE-ANY-POSITION
arms.note: a call read for more than its sign is rewritten, so a callback doing arithmetic on it sorts differently under a function of another magnitude

arms.name: M-SPLITP-MEMBER-SWAP
arms.note: the first part is read with the function for the text after the last delimiter, so a rewrite answers another text

arms.name: M-SPLITP-ANY-INDEX
arms.note: every index counts as the first part, so the second part, which no function of the utility reads, is rewritten

arms.name: M-SPLITP-EMPTY-DELIMITER
arms.note: an empty delimiter is accepted, so a split into characters is rewritten into the text before an empty string

arms.name: M-SPLITP-INTERPOLATED
arms.note: an interpolated delimiter is taken for a literal, so a delimiter the program computes, which may be empty, is rewritten

arms.name: M-SPLITP-ANY-RECEIVER
arms.note: every receiver is taken for a String, so an EReg or a nullable text is rewritten into a call that does not compile

arms.name: M-SPLITP-COMMENT
arms.note: a comment inside the cut is accepted, so the rewrite deletes it

arms.name: M-SPLITP-IMPORT-LOST
arms.note: the fix writes the short name of the utility and no import of its class, so the file stops compiling

arms.name: M-SPLITP-ANY-TOOLS
arms.note: any class is accepted as the utility, so the fix writes a call of a function that is missing or has another signature

arms.name: M-SPLITP-OVERLAPPING-POP
arms.note: a self-overlapping delimiter is accepted for the last part, so split and lastIndexOf, which pick different matches, are taken for one cut

arms.name: M-SPLITP-EXACT-PARAMS
arms.note: a utility function with a trailing optional parameter is refused as a configuration error

arms.name: M-SPLITP-ANY-SKIPPABLE
arms.note: a required third parameter is accepted, so the fix writes a two-argument call that does not compile

arms.name: M-REMEDY-COMPARE-UNSET
arms.note: a finding naming the project compare function carries no remedy module, so it is reported in a file whose build cannot resolve that function

arms.name: M-REMEDY-SPLIT-UNSET
arms.note: a finding naming the project text utility carries no remedy module, so it is reported in a file whose build cannot resolve that utility

arms.name: M-RCMP-ARROW-TAIL
arms.find: final tail: Null<QueryNode> = arrowTail(fn, body, s);
arms.note: an arrow block tail is not counted as returned, so a call there is reported without a fix

arms.name: M-RCMP-NULLABLE-IGNORED
arms.note: a function taking Null<T> is held to the non-null proof too, so a call over a maybe-null operand is reported without a fix

arms.name: M-RCMP-NULLABLE-ANY
arms.note: every named function is treated as taking Null<T>, so a function taking the plain type is fixed over a maybe-null operand

arms.name: M-RCMP-BARE-NULLABLE-IGNORED
arms.note: a bare Reflect.compare over a maybe-null element is reported without a fix even for a function taking Null<T>

arms.name: M-RCMP-HALF-NULLABLE-SIGNATURE
arms.note: a parameter that is not wrapped counts as wrapped, so a function taking Null<T> for one operand and T for the other is accepted and the fix writes a call that does not compile

arms.name: M-RCMP-FLOAT-KEY
arms.note: a Float key is refused as a configuration error, so Reflect.compare of two Floats is never moved to the named function

arms.name: M-PAC-ABSENT-FORM
arms.note: an absence test is written without its negation, so a not-found comparison reads as presence

arms.name: M-PAC-MIRROR
arms.note: a call on the right keeps the comparison unmirrored, so the sides-swapped forms read as their opposite

arms.name: M-PAC-ANY-RECEIVER
arms.note: every indexOf receiver counts as an Array, so a String or Dynamic one is rewritten

arms.name: M-PAC-FROM-INDEX
arms.note: an indexOf with a start index counts as the one-argument search

arms.name: M-PAC-ANY-BOUND
arms.find: return isNumber(node, ZERO, source, s) ? 0 : null;
arms.note: any other operand counts as zero, so an indexOf result compared with a variable reads as a membership test

arms.name: M-PAC-COMMENT
arms.note: a comment inside the comparison no longer blocks the rewrite, which would drop it

arms.name: M-JVMSC-ANY-PLACE
arms.note: every call is read as inside a short-circuit operand, the left operand and a bare condition included

arms.name: M-JVMSC-ANY-CALLEE
arms.note: every named call in an operand is flagged, not only a call to a declared inline function with a literal

arms.name: M-JVMSC-ANY-INLINE
arms.note: every local inline function is recorded, not only one whose body holds an object literal

arms.name: M-JVMSC-LAMBDA-BODY-IN-OPERAND
arms.note: a call inside a function literal in the operand is read as part of the short-circuit's own frame

arms.name: M-JVMSC-NULL-COALESCE-OPERAND
arms.note: the right operand of ?? is read as a short-circuit operand too

arms.name: M-RCMP-FLOAT-NAMED-CHAIN
arms.note: a Float chain stays silent even where the project names a Float function

arms.name: M-PCF-SUB-SILENT
arms.note: no subtraction is ever reported

arms.name: M-PCF-SUB-INT-ONLY
arms.note: a subtraction of Floats is reported like one of Ints

arms.name: M-PCF-SUB-ANY-OPERANDS
arms.note: a subtraction whose operands are not read from the two different parameters is reported

arms.name: M-PCF-SUB-ANY-CALL
arms.note: a two-parameter callback of any call is read as a comparator

arms.name: M-SCW-WALK-ANY-CALL
arms.note: the arguments of every call with a field callee are visited, not only those of sort

arms.name: M-SCW-COMPARATOR-ARITY
arms.note: a function literal is a comparator by any parameter count but two

arms.name: M-SCW-ELEMENT-INNER
arms.note: the element type is answered whole, so Null<T> elements answer Null<T> instead of Null

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-FIX-DROPPED
arms.note: every group's edits are dropped, so `duplicate-comparator` reports the duplicates and never extracts the static

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-SINGLE-SITE
arms.note: a comparator written at ONE sort call is reported as a duplicate of nothing

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-ELEMENT-BLIND
arms.note: the group key forgets the element type, so the same body over two element types is merged into one static

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-PARAMS-MERGED
arms.note: both parameters canonicalise to one mark, so the descending comparator joins the ascending one

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-CAPTURE-BLIND
arms.note: a lambda reading a local of its enclosing function counts as capture-free and is extracted into a static that cannot see it

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-UNRESOLVED-UNCOUNTED
arms.note: sites left alone for an unresolved element type are no longer counted, so the config note never says them

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-MACRO-FORM-DROPPED
arms.find: final keys: Null<Array<Key>> = key == null ? null : [key];
arms.note: a lambda comparing one key through Compare is read as a plain body: no macro form, and no merge with the Compare.asc call over the same key

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-ELEMENT-HOST-DROPPED
arms.find: if (onElement != null) return { host: onElement, why: '' };
arms.note: the element class the scope declares is never the host, so a cross-module group lands in the module holding most sites

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-CLASH-BLIND
arms.note: a host already declaring the name gets a second member of it

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-PACKAGES-BLIND
arms.note: a group spanning packages on an anonymous element is fixed into one package's module, which the other cannot import

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-IMPORTS-DROPPED
arms.note: a site module that does not import the host type gets the reference without the import

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-TYPE-PARAMETER-BLIND
arms.find: return owned != null && owned.exists(scope -> scope.from <= span.from && span.to <= scope.to);
arms.note: a type parameter element is grouped as a type, and the extracted static names a type parameter it cannot see

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-PARTIAL-GROUP
arms.note: a group is fixed with a suppressed site among it, so the suppressed lambda is rewritten too

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-UNSEEN-TYPE-BLIND
arms.note: a body naming a type the scope does not resolve is moved into a host that may not see it

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-KEYED-DEFAULTED
arms.replace: asc: macros[ASC] ?? { typePath: 'lib.Order', member: 'asc', nullable: false },
arms.note: an absent keyed option falls back to a built-in macro path, a hidden profile, and a key comparator takes a macro form the project never named

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-NULL-KEY-MACRO
arms.find: ordered: keys != null && (callback.value == null || orderedKeys(keys, element, entry.file, idx, s)),
arms.note: a key comparator over a Null<Int> key is extracted in the macro form, which refuses a nullable key at compile time

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-BROKEN-OPTION-RUNS
arms.note: a broken option is reported and the rule still runs on the files it governs, so a fix could call another function than the project named

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-KEYED-NOT-MACRO
arms.note: a keyed path naming a plain function is accepted as a key macro, and the extracted static calls it with key lambdas

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-THIS-BOUND
arms.note: a lambda reading this counts as capture-free and is extracted into a static that has no this

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-PRIVATE-HOST
arms.note: a private class becomes the host of a group with a site in another module, which cannot name it

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-HOST-OUTSIDE-RUN
arms.note: an element class outside the run's files is promised as the host, and the fix driver drops the whole group without saying why

arms.name: M-COPYM-ANY-COPY
arms.note: a copy method that takes a parameter is accepted as the named copy

arms.name: M-COPYM-ANY-ORDER
arms.note: a reordered, missing or extra argument is taken for the configured fields, so a different value is rewritten as a copy

arms.name: M-COPYM-ANY-RECEIVER
arms.note: arguments read off different receivers are taken for one value, so the copy takes both fields from one of them

arms.name: M-COPYM-ANY-TYPE
arms.note: a receiver of another type is rewritten as a copy, which converts a position instead

arms.name: M-COPYM-COMMENT
arms.note: a comment inside the construction is deleted by the rewrite

arms.name: M-COPYM-IMPURE
arms.note: a call or a getter among the arguments is dropped by the rewrite

arms.name: M-COPYM-NAMES-PAIR
arms.note: a construction of another type built from the same fields is rewritten as a copy of the configured type

arms.name: M-COPYM-OVERRIDE
arms.note: a copy method overridden in a subtype is still rewritten, which yields the subtype where the constructor yields the type

arms.name: M-COPYM-ONE-DECL
arms.note: a receiver of a same-named type from another package is rewritten to a copy of the configured type

arms.name: M-COPYM-FINAL
arms.note: a final type is refused whenever an unrelated type with an unresolvable ancestry overrides a method of that name

arms.name: M-COPYM-SELF-CALL
arms.note: the copy inside the copy method is rewritten to a call of that method, which calls itself

arms.name: M-INFER-FIELD-ONCE
arms.note: two parameters stored in one field are taken for two fields

arms.name: M-INFER-FIELD-TYPE
arms.note: a parameter stored into a field of another type, converting it, is taken for a plain copy

arms.name: M-INFER-FIELD-ACCESSOR
arms.note: a store through a setter, which runs code, is taken for a plain store

arms.name: M-INFER-COPY-FIELDS
arms.note: a copy that reads other fields than the constructor stores, or the same ones swapped, is taken for a copy

arms.name: M-INFER-COPY-ONE-STATEMENT
arms.note: a copy method that does more than return the construction is taken for a copy

arms.name: M-INFER-COPY-NEW-TYPE
arms.note: a method returning another type built from the same fields is taken for the copy

arms.name: M-INFER-GENERIC
arms.note: a generic type, whose construction infers its arguments, is taken for a plain one

arms.name: M-INFER-CTOR-PLAIN
arms.note: a constructor with a defaulted parameter is taken for one a copy fills in full

arms.name: M-INFER-ONE-COPY
arms.note: two proven copy methods leave the last one as the name the rewrite uses

arms.name: M-INFER-CONFIG-WINS
arms.note: a type the project configured is inferred as well, so a site the configuration does not name is rewritten

arms.name: M-INFER-SITE-FIELDS
arms.note: a construction passing the fields in another order than the constructor stores them is rewritten as a copy

arms.name: M-INFER-USED
arms.note: no pair is inferred from source, so a type the project did not configure is never rewritten

arms.name: M-INFER-CTOR-COUNT
arms.note: a constructor statement beyond the parameter stores, a call or a store of a non-parameter, is taken for a plain constructor

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-MESSAGE-COUNTS-GROUP
arms.find: message: 'the same comparator as other sort call(s) on ${site.element}
arms.replace: message: 'the same comparator as ${sites.length - 1} other sort call(s) on ${site.element}
arms.note: the finding names how many other sites its group holds, so a sort added in any file changes the text of every site's finding

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-MESSAGE-CARRIES-REFUSAL
arms.note: the finding's text carries the group's refusal, so a site joining from another package changes the text of every site's finding

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-REFUSED-SPELLING-COPIED
arms.replace: return type == null ? copiedOf(value, origin.source, build) : respelled(
arms.note: a compare function the grammar refuses to spell for the host is copied as the origin file spelled it, and the extracted body names another function than the source

arms.name: M-DUPCMP-NO-BUILDER-UNREPORTED
arms.find: if (build == null) return refused('the grammar builds no members');
arms.replace: if (build == null) return { name: named, slices: [], noFix: null, sites: sites };
arms.note: a grammar that builds no constructs leaves each group with no fix and no reason, so the unfixed ledger names nothing
